newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong says Q1 sales hurt by U.S. dollar.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong says Q1 sales hurt by U.S. dollar.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc said Monday that the strength of the U.S. dollar hurt sales in some segments in the first quarter.

Overall sales in the first quarter were $518.3 million, a 3.4 percent increase from the prior year's $501.2 million. Excluding the translation effect of the stronger U.S. dollar, sales growth would have been 4.3 percent, the company said.
Worldwide sales dropped 2.6 percent but would have increased 2.6 percent without the translation effects of the U.S. dollar.
Building product sales would rose 3.9 percent. Excluding the effect of the dollar, sales would have increased by 4.9 percent, it said.

In Europe, sales declined 4.1 percent principally because of the dollar's strength, as well as "continued relatively weak market conditions and competitive pressures in the buliding and industry products segments," the company said in a statement.

The company's worldwide floor coverings sales increased 5.2 percent. Armstrong attributed the increase to continuing improvement in U.S. home center and commercial sales, modest growth in North American residential sheet flooring and the effect of the new line of laminate flooring.
